words.enExample: Small wins cement the new habit.
words.note: 💡 本义水泥。搭 cement a habit。微习惯靠重复 cement。

words.enExample: Tie the habit to a stable cue like brushing teeth.
words.zhExample: 把习惯绑在一个稳定线索上，比如刷牙。
words.note: 💡 搭 a cue。习惯回路：cue → routine → reward。

words.enExample: Stack a new habit onto an old one.
words.zhExample: 把新习惯叠在旧习惯上。
words.note: 💡 搭 stack habits。habit stacking 是低阻力养成法。

words.enExample: One lapse does not erase the streak.
words.zhExample: 一次中断，不抹掉此前的连续。
words.note: 💡 搭 a lapse。掉链子叫 lapse，别因此放弃。

words.enExample: A 30-day streak makes the habit stick.
words.note: 💡 搭 keep a streak。微习惯靠 streak 产生复利。

essay.title: Tiny Habits, Lasting Change
essay.author: 佚名
paragraphs: We dream of big changes and then wait for the day we feel ready to begin. That day rarely comes, because a large goal feels like a wall we must scale all at once. The trick is to make the first step so small that it stops feeling like a beginning.

A tiny habit asks almost nothing of you. Two minutes of reading. One push-up against the wall. A single sentence written before the coffee cools. Each is so small it feels almost foolish to refuse, and that is exactly the point.

Momentum is built sideways, not upward. You do not leap into a new self; you nudge the old one a few degrees, day after day, until the direction is different enough to notice. Small actions repeated are not small; they are how a life quietly redraws its lines.

The danger is impatience. We start small, feel nothing, and quit before the compound effect has a chance to show. But a habit is a loan to your future self, and the interest is paid in a currency you only learn to read later.

So pick one ridiculously small thing and do it every day this week. Not to impress anyone, not to prove a point, but to prove to yourself that you can keep a promise to no one but you. The change that lasts is the one that started too small to fear.
translations: 我们向往巨大的改变，然后等着哪天「准备好了」再开始。那一天很少到来，因为宏大的目标像一堵墙，仿佛必须一口气翻过去。诀窍在于，把第一步做得足够小，小到它不再像一个开端。
一个微习惯几乎不向你索取什么。读两分钟书。对着墙做一个俯卧撑。在咖啡凉掉之前写下一句话。每一件都小到拒绝它简直显得傻，而这恰恰就是关键。
势头是横着积累起来的，不是往上跳出来的。你不是一跃成为全新的自己；你只是把旧的自己每天推几度，日复一日，直到方向变得明显不同。被反复做的小动作并不小；它们正是一个生命悄悄重画自身轮廓的方式。
危险在于没耐心。我们从小处着手，却什么感觉也没有，于是在复利效应有机会显现之前就放弃了。但习惯是借给未来自己的钱，而利息，是用一种你后来才学会辨认的货币支付的。
所以，挑一件小到荒谬的事，这个星期每天都做。不为惊艳谁，也不为证明什么，只为向自己证明：你能对一个除了你之外谁也不欠的人信守承诺。能长久的改变，恰恰是那个小到让人不怕的开始。

grammar.example: The trick is to make the first step so small that it stops feeling like a beginning.
grammar.note: so...that... 表示「如此…以至于…」，so 修饰形容词 small，that 引导结果从句说明「小」带来的后果——它不再像一个开端。这种结构常用来解释做法为何有效。 举一反三：同类如 make it so easy that you cannot say no、keep it so short that it fits anywhere。

grammar.point: 分号对照：do not leap; (but) nudge
grammar.example: You do not leap into a new self; you nudge the old one a few degrees, day after day.
grammar.note: 分号连接两个对照分句：do not leap（不跳跃）与 nudge...day after day（日复一日轻推）。but 在此被分号与语义替代，强调「渐变」对「突变」的取代，正是微习惯的核心理念。 举一反三：也可写成 you do not leap but nudge，或 not by a leap but by a nudge。

grammar.point: that 引导定语从句修饰抽象先行词
grammar.example: The change that lasts is the one that started too small to fear.
grammar.note: 两个 that 引导的定语从句分别修饰 the change 与 the one（指代 change）。lasts 与 started 都是定语从句谓语，把「持久的」与「始于小到不怕的」两个属性直接挂到名词后，句式对称而有力。 举一反三：同类如 the habit that sticks is the one that costs almost nothing。

vocab.enExample: He scaled the wall in seconds with a boost.
vocab.zhExample: 他借力几秒钟就翻过了那堵墙。
vocab.note: 用法：原义秤或鳞片，动词指攀上或越过墙、山

vocab.enExample: Two push-ups a day is still a habit worth keeping.
vocab.zhExample: 每天两个俯卧撑，也仍是值得保持的习惯。
vocab.note: 用法：以手臂撑地的力量练习

vocab.enExample: It would be foolish to refuse such a small step.
vocab.zhExample: 拒绝这么小的一步，才显得傻。
vocab.note: 用法：显得荒唐或不聪明

vocab.enExample: Once started, the momentum carried her through.
vocab.zhExample: 一旦开始，那股势头便带着她走了下去。
vocab.note: 用法：运动或进展中积累的冲力

vocab.enExample: She nudged the project forward with one small edit.
vocab.zhExample: 她用一处小修改，把项目往前推了一推。
vocab.note: 用法：用小力促成缓慢移动或改变

vocab.enExample: The year redrew the map of his daily life.
vocab.zhExample: 这一年重画了他日常生活的地图。
vocab.note: 用法：重新描绘线条或边界，过去式 redrew

vocab.enExample: Small compound gains beat big sudden ones.
vocab.zhExample: 微小而累积的收获，胜过突然而巨大的。
vocab.note: 用法：效果层层叠加、越积越大

vocab.enExample: He set a ridiculous goal: one page a month.
vocab.zhExample: 他定了个荒唐的目标：一个月一页。
vocab.note: 用法：小到或怪到令人发笑
